body.text: UKPNP International Conference on Jammu Kashmir in House of Commons UK --- 8th July 2025

London, 8 July 2025 --- The United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP) held a landmark International Kashmir Conference in the Boothroyd Room of the Houses of Parliament, London, under the theme: 'Kashmir Conflict: Peace, Security and Fundamental Rights in Jammu and Kashmir'. The conference saw extensive participation from Members of the British Parliament, international human rights activists, legal experts, academics, Kashmiri and oppressed nations' leaders, media professionals, and diaspora representatives.

body.caption: Complete Video of the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference at House of Commons, London --- 8th July 2025
Panelists at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri, Exiled Chairman of UKPNP and Administrative Director of CIRAC to the United Nations (Geneva & New York), was the chief guest and keynote speaker. In his powerful address, he expressed sincere gratitude to Labour MP Richard Burgon for hosting this important conference, and to Fabian Hamilton for initiating this vital platform. He stated that UKPNP is honored to hold the 4th International UKPNP Kashmir Conference in the British Parliament, advancing peace, democracy, and human rights in South Asia.

body.caption: Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri addressing the conference

body.text: From the outset, UKPNP has championed secularism, peace, democracy, and reunification of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir, while categorically rejecting the use of religion as a weapon, all forms of extremism, terrorism, and proxy politics.

Due to this pro-people and pro-peace ideology, UKPNP has faced state persecution and was forced into exile but remains committed to its cause. Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri strongly condemned the extrajudicial killings of Zarnosh Nasim and Jibran Nasim, two educated brothers from Bagh, Azad Kashmir, who were reportedly killed in a police operation in Rawalakot. UKPNP demands an independent judicial inquiry and full accountability for this grave human rights violation.

The conference was hosted by Richard Burgon MP, Labour MP for Leeds East and Former Shadow Secretary of State for Justice. Other distinguished MPs present included Fabian Hamilton MP, Labour MP for Leeds North East and Former Shadow Minister for Peace and Disarmament; Imran Hussain MP, Labour MP for Bradford East and Chair of the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Kashmir; and Ian Byrne MP, Labour MP for Liverpool West Derby.

body.caption: Distinguished MPs and Panelists at the UKPNP International Kashmir Conference, House of Commons, London

body.text: MP Richard Burgon emphasized that Kashmir is one of the world's longest unresolved conflicts, which must be resolved peacefully according to the will of the Kashmiri people. MP Fabian Hamilton stated that this conference should ideally be the last if it leads to peace, and committed continued support to Kashmiris' right to self-determination. MP Imran Hussain declared the Kashmir conflict as an international — not a bilateral issue — rejecting the relevance of the Shimla Agreement. MP Ian Byrne reaffirmed that self-determination is a fundamental right which Kashmiris deserve.
Call for Reunification and Buffer State Status

Kashmir is not a territorial dispute between India and Pakistan — it is a matter of life, identity, and dignity for millions of Kashmiris. We demand freedom of expression, movement, reunification, and the right to self-determination for all.

Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri urged Great Britain and the international community to support the establishment of a unified, independent buffer state of Jammu and Kashmir — one that serves peace and development in South Asia and denies its land for use in aggression against any neighbor.

body.caption: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan, Central Spokesperson UKPNP — Moderator of the Conference

body.text: UKPNP leadership thanked MP Richard Burgon for hosting the impactful conference and all MPs for their insights. Moderator Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan thanked MPs Richard Burgon and Fabian Hamilton, noting that this was the 4th consecutive international conference on Kashmir organized by UKPNP in the House of Commons. Special congratulations were extended to the United Kingdom Chapter of UKPNP for their remarkable efforts, dedicated coordination, and powerful presence in organizing this successful event.

Jammu and Kashmir is not a territorial or bilateral issue between India and Pakistan. It is an international issue. United Nations resolutions on Kashmir remain relevant and take precedence over the Tashkent and Shimla Agreements, or any other bilateral arrangements between the two countries.

The entire State of Jammu and Kashmir, including the Kashmir Valley, Jammu, Ladakh, Azad Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan, constitutes one historical and political entity and remains disputed. India and Pakistan have no legal right to annex, merge, or unilaterally determine the status of any part of the historical State of Jammu and Kashmir. The people of the State of Jammu and Kashmir deserve their fundamental rights, including the right to free movement, the right to reunification of divided families, and the right to self-determination in accordance with international law and United Nations resolutions.

The future status of Jammu and Kashmir must be determined in accordance with United Nations resolutions and in line with the wishes and aspirations of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Any decision imposed on the basis of majoritarianism or military force is illegal, constitutes a clear violation of United Nations resolutions on Kashmir and international law, and is unacceptable to the people of the disputed State of Jammu and Kashmir.

In conclusion, the UKPNP reaffirmed its peaceful and democratic mission for the reunification of Jammu and Kashmir. The event marked a significant milestone in uniting global voices for peace, justice, and fundamental rights in South Asia.
